Step 3b instrument mismatch, resolved against the data rather than the name. The table's seven codes are NOT the seven GAD-7 items. Rows of the analysed file (supp-6, peerj-14-20868-s006.xlsx, which data/han_2026_gad7.py melts unchanged) were paired cell-for-cell with the study's administered questionnaire file (supp-2, s002.xlsx, titled by PeerJ 'Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scales administered to the elderly population in Jiangsu Province') using rows whose PHQ-9 nine-tuple is unique in both files (217 rows). Every GAD code matched exactly one questionnaire column at 100% (best rival <= 0.79). Result: (a) GAD02 is 'Excessively worrying about various things' and GAD03 is 'Unable to stop or control worrying', i.e. the administration reverses canonical GAD-7 items 2 and 3, and the paper's Table 2 labels them the canonical way round (GAD2 'Uncontrollable worry', GAD3 'Excessive worry') -- the labels are wrong for this data, the means are not (0.23/0.20 matched to both); (b) GAD07 is not an anxiety item at all: the administered form has no 'feeling afraid as if something awful might happen' item, and its seventh column is a loss-of-interest question answered No/Cannot judge/Yes, stored 0/1/2. The paper nonetheless calls it 'Fear something awful Feeling afraid' and sums it into GAD_Score; its network predictability (0.131 vs 0.60-0.72 for the other six) is consistent with it not belonging. Because GAD07 sits on a 3-level No/Cannot judge/Yes coding while GAD01-GAD06 sit on the 0-3 frequency scale, the response table mixes two scales -- a property of the source data, not of the item text. instructions left blank: neither the questionnaire file, the codebook nor the paper reproduces a stem sentence, so none was invented. option_text holds the study's own English value labels because no Chinese option wording appears anywhere in the deposit; option_text_translated is therefore deliberately blank while item_text is the administered Chinese from codebook supp-10 (s010.docx) with the authors' English in item_text_translated. No rights restriction on GAD-7 wording found or quotable (the PHQ/GAD screener family is distributed with no permission required); the article is CC BY 4.0. ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK (Step 5b): the GAD07 finding is CONFIRMED against live data via item_stats.R, independently of the agent's row-pairing. GAD01-GAD06 all run min 0 / max 3 with ceiling_pct 0.0-0.3, while GAD07 runs min 0 / max 2 with ceiling_pct 13.8 -- a different number of levels and a distribution nothing like its six neighbours. That confirms the response table mixes two scales and that GAD07 is not a fourth-option frequency item. Per-item means are as reported (GAD02 0.23, GAD03 0.20), so the paper's Table 2 means do match the columns while its labels for items 2 and 3 do not; means alone cannot separate that pair, which is why the agent's S2 row-pairing (100% vs a best rival of 0.79) is the load-bearing evidence and was left as the primary route.

Clean pass with three disclosed caveats. (1) RESPONSE CODING IS NOT UNIFORM ACROSS ITEMS. The raw survey file (S1 File, peerj-14-20868-s001.xlsx) records every ISI rating as option position 1-5 while its own column headers state the anchors as 0-4; the merged deposit file the IRW table is built from (S6 File) shifted ISI01 and ISI07 down by one and left ISI02-ISI06 on the raw 1-5 codes, so live ISI01/ISI07 run 0-4 and live ISI02-ISI06 run 1-5. option_text is mapped accordingly: the lowest anchor sits at resp=0 for ISI01/ISI07 and at resp=1 for ISI02-ISI06. This is a property of the deposited data, not a transcription choice -- the study's own script (S3 File, lines 105-107) intended a uniform -1 on all seven columns and the result was only partly carried through; ISI_Score in the deposit is the uncorrected sum (min 4, max 33, mean 9.47) and the paper reports that same 9.5 (SD 5.8) against a stated 0-28 range. (2) THREE ITEMS SHIP ENGLISH IN THE BASE FIELD. ISI01-ISI03 are the three components of a single composite severity question ('1,1,1'-style cell split in S3 File lines 84-88); the deposit publishes the shared Chinese stem (shipped as section_prompt) but never the three sub-domain labels in any language, so item_text for those three carries the paper's own English domain wording ('difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, early morning awakenings', Methods) with item_text_translated left empty -- the documented fallback, applied to 3 of 7 rows. option_text is English throughout for the same reason: the anchors exist only inside the English column headers of S1 File, never in Chinese. ISI04-ISI07 ship the administered Chinese verbatim from S10 File with the authors' own English in item_text_translated. (3) THE PAPER'S OWN TABLE 2 LABELS CONTRADICT ITS OWN ANALYSIS SCRIPT for ISI05/ISI06/ISI07. Table 2 names them 'Noticeability of sleep problems by others', 'Distress caused by sleep difficulties' and 'Interference with daytime functioning' -- canonical ISI item order -- while S3 File lines 92-94 rename by an exact colnames() match, giving ISI05 = daily-life impact, ISI06 = prominence vs other quality-of-life factors, ISI07 = anxious/worried. The study's questionnaire simply asked the last three in a different order from the canonical ISI. The shipped text follows the script and the raw column headers, which is a by-name tie; the Table 2 labels are a descriptor list the authors wrote. Only ISI01-ISI04 are unaffected. Other checks: only the two endpoints of each 5-point scale are anchored in the source, so the interior levels carry blank option_text rather than being padded. ISI03 has 3 respondents coded 0, an out-of-range code present in the raw file too (3 cases there as well) with no anchor; no option row is emitted for it. The questionnaire's recall window is 'the past two weeks' while the paper's Methods describes the ISI as covering the past month. Rights: no quotable restriction found -- the shipped wording is this study's own adapted Chinese questionnaire and the authors' own English, published in a CC BY 4.0 PeerJ article and its supplements, not a transcription of the Morin ISI form; Mapi Research Trust distributes the ISI but no fee or no-redistribution clause could be quoted, and silence is permission. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED (orchestrator, Step 5c): audit_batch flags '60% of rows have blank option_text' and 'ISI03(0) has no option_text row'. Neither is an itemtext defect. The 60% is the source's own anchoring: the questionnaire labels only the two endpoints of each 5-point scale, so 3 of 5 levels per item are legitimately unlabelled and are left blank rather than padded with their own number, per SKILL.md. The ISI03(0) gap is a RESPONSE-DATA defect, not a text gap: 3 of 2086 respondents carry an out-of-range 0 on an item whose live scale is 1-5, and the same 3 out-of-range cases are present in the raw deposit, so no anchor exists or should be invented for it. ORCHESTRATOR RE-CHECK (Step 5b): the non-uniform coding claim is CONFIRMED against live data via item_stats.R -- ISI01 min/max 0/4 (mean 0.69), ISI07 0/4 (mean 0.54), ISI02/04/05/06 all 1/5 (means 1.57-1.84), ISI03 0/5 only because of those 3 stray zeroes. The ~1-point mean gap between the two shifted items and the other five is exactly the off-by-one the note describes.
